page.layout: One page of text. Running head across the top with the page number at the top left. Below the head, the running text in one column with a chapter heading and an italic argument summary, ending with a catchword at the bottom right.

main_text.p: pisse Hebræis, neque Galatis tantùm sed Cappadocibus, sed Bythyniis, sed Ponti-cis, sed Asiaticis, & quidem de tali argu-mento, quale Petrus exequitur, non quale Paulus ad Galatas. Secundò excipi possent, quæ contrà Epistolæ authoritatem motæ partim ἀντιλογίᾳ, partim ἐνισταμέναι, partim ἀπόρως, tantùm abest ut Paulinam illa sapientiam redoleat; Nisi res nobis cum iis qui authorem, non verò authoritatem Epistolæ in dubium vocant, nisi etiam inanissima hæc tela olim hodieque in contorquentium capita Theologi retorsissent, de quibus aliquid in parte ἀνασκευαστικῶς.
main_text.head: CAPUT V.

head.i: Quartum argumentum à testimonio divino. Paulinarum τὰ δυσνόητα. Respicit Petrus Epistolam ad Hebræos. Probatur. Difficultates illius sigillatim excussa. De interitu Apostatarum. De Melchisedeco. Non expediunt se Interpretes. Sententiarum omnium nodi. De Christi sacerdotio &c. De ἀναλογοφανίαι quibusdam. Centor

page.notes: Greek words are printed in italic and are hard to read at this scan resolution. The Greek in the summary (τὰ δυσνόητα, ἀναλογοφανίαι) and in the first paragraph (ἀντιλογίᾳ, ἐνισταμέναι, ἀπόρως, ἀνασκευαστικῶς) are my best reading and should be checked against the original. The catchword "sére" is at the bottom right and is probably the first word of the next page. The first word of the continued paragraph is cut off at the left edge and is read as "pisse", which may be part of "Epistole". The running head is partly blurred and "Epistole" may be "Epistolæ".
